subject: Accented letters appears in species name tags

messages.author: 801722d43588a5ba
messages.subject: Accented letters appears in species name tags
parts:
Hi all,

I am unable to figure out why accented letters appear in some of my species tags when I process images using camtrapR. For example, Panthera tigris appears as PantheraÁ tigris, or Hyaena hyaena appears as HyaenaÁ hyaena. I performed a check on these images in Digikam and it looks fine. In fact, I went ahead and retagged these images just to be extra sure but the problem continued to exist. 

This is a major issue as I am not able to proceed further with the creation of detection histories both using the given species tag or the accented one that appears, for example, in my record table.

Any help or insights will be much appreciated. 

Thanks in advance,
Saloni Salaria

messages.author: 0b86ca0cb4b615b0
messages.subject: Re: Accented letters appears in species name tags
parts:
Hi Saloni,
I haven't encountered this issue before, and I believe it might have to do with your machine's locale settings, not digiKam or camtrapR.
Would you mind sharing the output of 
sessionInfo() please?
Also, you can run exifTagNames() and share the line with "HierarchicalSubject". That is where camtrapR reads the species tage (and other tags) from, and if the accent is not there, then digiKam is innocent and it is somehow added in R. If in doubt, feel free to share some images (zipped to preserve metadata).

Alternatively, a quick workaround would be to just remove the character with gsub():

> x <- c("PantheraÁ tigris", "HyaenaÁ hyaena")
> gsub("Á", "", x)
[1] "Panthera tigris" "Hyaena hyaena"  

Best regards,
Jürgen

Thank you for the data. In the metadata you shared, in HierarchicalSubject, I see "Species_ID|Panthera tigris, Individual_ID|KAZI_107_M, Camera|CamB", so that is correct as far as I can tell, meaning digiKam does its job properly and the metadata are clean, from what I see. Feel free to share an image in a zip and I will double check. It could potentially be something in camtrapR.

But it looks like R reads out correct metadata from the images and in processing them for some reason adds this extra character. It is really quite odd, since your R locale setting also seem fine (English, US). I'm puzzled.

Also, have you tried it on a different computer yet, can you reproduce it there? I have a feeling it might have to do with your machine somehow, but I don't know why. Also, consider updating your R, even though I feel it is unlikely to fix the issue. And what is the output of options()$encoding? You could try running your code again after declaring options(encoding = "UTF-8"), but that is just a wild guess.

And yes, the workaround was for the after you create the record tables, but of course I understand you'd rather avoid this issue altogether.

Let me know how it goes with the suggestions.
Jürgen

messages.author: 0b86ca0cb4b615b0
messages.subject: Re: Accented letters appears in species name tags
parts:
For anyone interested in the topic, it was an issue with character encoding. I don't understand where it originated from, but there's a fix. From version 2.0.3 (on github already) you can add "L" to additionalMetadataTags (in recordTable / recordTableIndividual) which will make Exiftool read characters with the latin character set (instead of UTF-8).  That solved the issue.

recordTable(..., additionalMetadataTags = "L")

We tested it and it extracted the correct species names (currently there still is a warning about "column 'L' is missing", which you can safely ignore). You can still add other values to additionalMetadataTags as usual.
Jürgen

Hey all,

My question is in continuation of the accented character issue. Setting additional metadata tags removes the accented character from Species and Metadata columns in record table, but if I wish to append species names to my images, it again attached accented character to the images. So I decided to use the record table to append species names, which I did successfully, but when I try to open the files it says the following. Any idea how to fix this. 


My code is below:
library(devtools)
install_github("jniedballa/camtrapR") 
library(camtrapR)
setwd("C:/")
Sys.which("exiftool") 

images <- file.path("C:\\Users\\saloni\\Desktop\\Hyaena", "images")
length(list.files(images, pattern = "JPG", recursive = TRUE)) ## Total number of images.

RT <- recordTable(inDir  = images,
                  IDfrom = "metadata",
                  metadataSpeciesTag = "Species_ID",
                  additionalMetadataTag = "L")
    
library(tidyr)
Name     <- separate(data = RT, col = FileName, sep = ".JPG", into = "Name", remove = FALSE, extra = "drop")
NewName  <- unite(data = Name, col= NewName, c(Name, Species), remove = FALSE, sep = "__")

## Create vector of new files
new_files <- paste0("C:\\Users\\saloni\\Desktop\\Hyaena\\", NewName$NewName, ".JPG")
new_files

## Copy from old files to new files
file.copy(from = images, to = new_files)
